svg.title: libdes architecture
svg.desc: A des::network, seeded once, holds the nodes, a next-event heap, the per-class routing matrix and flow statistics. Here the nodes form a central server model: a source, a processor-sharing CPU, a FIFO disk and a sink; after each CPU burst a job of class c visits the disk with probability p[c], then returns to the CPU, and otherwise leaves through the sink. Each simulation step takes the node with the earliest departure from the heap, lets its next job depart, samples the next node from the routing matrix and hands the job to that node, which puts it in a free server or a waiting queue. The source keeps one pending arrival per class and draws the inter-arrival times from a distribution per class. The sink absorbs jobs on arrival and never enters the heap. Every node draws from its own block of random streams of one xoshiro256** generator: stream 0 for its choices among queues and servers, stream 1 + c for the times of class c; the routing out of node i draws from the next block, one stream per class. Every queue delegates admission and ordering to a policy, which creates the job store holding its jobs: fifo a sequence_store (ring buffer), is a time_store (binary heap), ps a ps_store (heap in virtual time). Observers attached to node signals receive the event fields as a message and keep per-class statistics across runs.
svg.text: a central server model: after each CPU burst, a class c job visits the disk with probability p[c]
all jobs in service at once
One seed; long_jump() cuts blocks of 2¹⁹² draws, jump() streams of 2¹²⁸.
